newsitem.title: GERMANY: High joblessness justifies high '97 deficit-Waigel.
newsitem.headline: High joblessness justifies high '97 deficit-Waigel.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Friday Germany's high unemployment justified an increase in the 1997 budget deficit contained in the 1997 supplementary budget.
"The high unemployment justifies the rise in the 1997 deficit," Waigel told a news conference after Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet approved the 1997 supplementary budget.
The cabinet approved Waigel's 461 billion mark ($263 billion) draft budget for 1998 and a supplementary budget for 1997 that enlarges the deficit.

The supplementary budget for this year raises the projected deficit to 71.2 billion marks from an original plan of 53.3 billion, but the government has said it still expects to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU).

The cabinet approval sets the stage for parliamentary debate on the bills, expected in special sessions in August or September. Opposition Social Democrats have already attacked the government bills as shaky and lacking in credibility.

Since the 1997 deficit exceeds government investment, the government must now, under the constitution, make a declaration that the excessive deficit is being used to combat an imbalance in the economy.
